item.text: I’ll audit this strictly as a fresh-reader critique, separating definitional/context gaps from actual algebraic inconsistencies. I’ll also recompute the quadratic solve, every geometric-series simplification, and the displayed degree-five evaluations rather than treating the prose’s checks as evidence.

The quadratic computation is internally correct, as are the explicit geometric-series simplifications and the arithmetic of the two degree-five final formulas. The main problems are missing definitions and cross-references, an incomplete degree-five derivation, a broken paragraph, conflation of algorithmic depth with coefficient precision, and a genuine tension between the claimed denominator theorem and the still-open determinant condition.

1. “Splitting type \(\sigma\)” is never defined. A fresh reader must infer that it is a multiset of ramification/residue-degree pairs \(\{(e_i,f_i)\}\) satisfying \(\sum e_if_i=n\). It is also unstated whether multiplicities are retained and how inseparable or repeated-root polynomials are treated.

2. The ambient probability space is introduced indirectly. It should be made explicit somewhere before the first count that the coefficients range independently over \(\mathbb Z_p\), so the space is \(\mathbb Z_p^n\).

3. “One number per prime” is imprecise: there is one number per prime, degree, and splitting type.

4. “Every polynomial in [a cylinder] has splitting type \(\sigma\)” presupposes that splitting type is locally constant off the discriminant locus. That fact is essential to the construction but is not stated or cited here.

5. The special rule declaring any cylinder containing a repeated-root polynomial “undecided” is stronger than merely requiring two different types in the cylinder. The reason for this convention should be stated; otherwise it appears ad hoc.

6. The partition
   \[
   \sum_\sigma D_\sigma(k)+U(k)=p^{nk}
   \]
   is correct under that convention, provided the collection of types is finite and exhaustive. Neither point has yet been established when the formula appears.

7. The monotonicity argument is correct but slightly compressed: it is the fractions, not the raw counts, that satisfy
   \[
   \frac{D_\sigma(k+1)}{p^{n(k+1)}}\geq
   \frac{D_\sigma(k)}{p^{nk}},
   \]
   because each decided cylinder has \(p^n\) decided children.

8. Formula \((0)\) is internally correct. The upper bound follows because only descendants of cylinders already decided to \(\sigma\), or of currently undecided cylinders, can eventually contribute to \(\sigma\).

9. The prose reverses the logical order around \((0)\). The limit defining \(\rho_\sigma(p)\) already exists by bounded monotonicity; \(U(k)/p^{nk}\to0\) is needed to identify the complementary upper approximation and obtain exhaustiveness, not to make that individual limit exist.

10. “It does, geometrically in \(k\)” overstates what is later displayed. The eventual certified bound has a polynomial factor times a geometric factor. It is exponentially decaying, but not literally a pure geometric sequence.

11. “Computable to any precision at a finite level” requires an effective method for computing or bounding \(U(k)\). The semantic definition of \(U(k)\)—quantifying over every \(p\)-adic polynomial in a cylinder—is not by itself a finite algorithm.

12. Two different notions of undecidedness are later used without a clean separation: true-type undecided cylinders from the opening, and the classifier’s undecided states. Their equality or comparison is precisely part of the unproved faithfulness/exhaustiveness material.

13. Equality with Haar probability is valid once almost every polynomial is eventually decided. Saying “the measure theory is spent” hides the required facts that the discriminant-zero locus is null and that the increasing union of decided cylinders exhausts the type event up to that null set.

14. The first “Theorem (uniformity)” is not presently a theorem according to the status paragraphs that immediately follow it. It should be unmistakably labelled as the target or conjecture; calling it a theorem before restricting the proved cases is misleading.

15. The ring
   \[
   \mathbb Q\!\left[q,\frac1q,\frac1{q^c-1}\;(c\ge1)\right]
   \]
   is coherent, and the assertion that its permitted denominator factors do not vanish for real \(q\ge2\) is correct. It does not, however, follow merely from the listed elementary operations that an arbitrary matrix inverse remains in this ring; that requires the later “master denominator theorem.”

16. “At every prime power \(q=p^\delta\)” changes the coefficient ring from \(\mathbb Z_p\) to the integers of an unramified extension. That ring and the valuation normalization should be named.

17. Terms such as “development,” “kernel,” “capstone,” “classifier,” “three certified readings,” “instance data,” “regularity gate,” “falsifier,” and “hypothesis slots” presuppose an external formalization that is never identified. A reader needs the proof assistant, artifact/repository, definitions, and certificate boundaries.

18. “Machine-checked at every prime” is ambiguous. It could mean one parametric proof or infinitely many evaluations; those are very different claims.

19. The thirteen reserved hypotheses are described as “currently trivially satisfiable.” That makes the present implication potentially vacuous or unconstraining. Until the hypotheses are formulated, it is unclear what mathematical content the capstone actually certifies.

20. The quadratic theorem’s three formulas are mutually consistent:
   \[
   \frac1{q+1}+2\frac{q}{2(q+1)}=1,
   \]
   and all three specialize to \(1/3\) at \(q=2\).

21. The odd-prime discriminant classification is correct for a separable monic quadratic: even valuation plus square unit gives split, even valuation plus nonsquare unit gives the unramified quadratic field, and odd valuation gives a ramified field.

22. Both odd-prime geometric sums are correct:
   \[
   (1-q^{-1})\sum_{j\ge0}q^{-(2j+1)}=\frac1{q+1},
   \]
   and
   \[
   \frac12(1-q^{-1})\sum_{j\ge0}q^{-2j}
   =\frac{q}{2(q+1)}.
   \]

23. The \(p=2\) case division is correct. Conditional on \(b\) even, the probabilities are
   \[
   \frac23\cdot\frac14=\frac16
   \]
   for each of split and inert, leaving \(2/3\) ramified. Including the \(b\)-parity weights gives \(1/3\) for each type.

24. The table for the \(p=2\) calculation is malformed Markdown: the data rows lack leading and trailing pipes and therefore may not render as a table.

25. “Only \(\mathbb Q_2(\sqrt5)\) is unramified” means only one of the seven nontrivial quadratic extensions, up to isomorphism. That qualification should be explicit.

26. “The product formula of the tame expandable above” and later references to “the first expandable” and “the cubic table in the first expandable” have no corresponding object in the supplied statement. These are broken cross-references.

27. The claim that a repeated linear cluster becomes “a fresh, smaller copy” with independent uniform coefficients is a nontrivial measure-preserving Hensel-coordinate statement, not a consequence of recentering alone. It needs a precise lemma.

28. The claim that a repeated factor of degree \(d>1\) is handled simply by replacing \(q\) with \(q^d\) suppresses descent and conjugacy constraints. A fresh reader cannot tell whether the computation is being performed over the unramified extension and then descended, or directly over \(\mathbb Z_p\).

29. The residual-polynomial formula is internally consistent:
   \[
   R_S(y)=\sum_{j=0}^d
   \left(\frac{c_{i_0+je}}{p^{v_0-jh}}\bmod p\right)y^j.
   \]
   The exponents are integers at the segment’s lattice points, and coefficients strictly above the segment reduce to zero.

30. The letter \(f\) is overloaded: it denotes the original polynomial and later the residue degree \(f=\deg\varphi_i\). This is especially confusing in “an irreducible piece of \(f\) with \(e\ldots\) and \(f=\deg\varphi_i\).”

31. The statement that a simple residual factor immediately certifies an irreducible piece relies on the precise Newton-polygon factorization theorem and its regularity hypotheses. Those hypotheses are not stated.

32. The polygon of \(x^3+2x^2+4\) is correct. At \(i=2\), the segment has height \(2/3\), while the coefficient point has height \(1\), so it lies strictly above the hull.

33. The conclusion that this cubic is irreducible is correct: a root valuation with reduced denominator \(3\) forces the degree of any containing irreducible factor to be divisible by \(3\), exhausting the total degree.

34. Both quartic residual expansions are correct:
   \[
   x^4+18:\quad R(y)=y^2+2=y^2-1,
   \]
   and
   \[
   x^4+9:\quad R(y)=y^2+1,
   \]
   irreducible over \(\mathbb F_3\). The displayed factorizations with \(s^2=-2\) are also algebraically correct.

35. The phrase “\(2\mid e\) for every piece” is confusing because the same paragraph has just fixed the segment denominator \(e=2\). What is meant is that every resulting factor has ramification index divisible by \(2\).

36. The cylinder mass for the cubic polygon is correct:
   \[
   (1-q^{-1})q^{-2}\cdot q^{-2}\cdot q^{-1}
   =(1-q^{-1})q^{-5},
   \]
   which equals \(1/64\) at \(q=2\).

37. Formula \((\dagger)\),
   \[
   R'(y)=y^\mu h(y+\tilde c),
   \]
   is algebraically correct at the stated first residual level: it is just the substitution into
   \(R(y)=(y-\tilde c)^\mu h(y)\). Its applicability at deeper Newton levels requires the omitted normalization and anchor data.

38. “No new randomness enters at a descent” is too broad. The immediately transported leading row is determined by existing digits, but later rows plainly contain fresh coefficient digits. The intended scope of the statement is unclear.

39. Formula \((\ddagger)\) is correct modulo \(2\). The sign from \(1-u=-4u_2+\cdots\) disappears in \(\mathbb F_2\), and
   \[
   u_2+t+t^2=u_2
   \]
   because \(t^2=t\) in \(\mathbb F_2\).

40. The two consequences of \((\ddagger)\) are correct: \(u\equiv5\bmod8\) produces residual \(y^2+y+1\), while \(u\equiv1\bmod8\) is the square case.

41. The multiplication formula in
   \[
   D=\kappa[u]/(u^e-\bar z)
   \]
   is correct for representatives \(0\le\rho,\sigma<e\):
   \[
   u^\rho u^\sigma
   =\bar z^{\lfloor(\rho+\sigma)/e\rfloor}
     u^{(\rho+\sigma)\bmod e}.
   \]
   But calling this “the one ring” obscures that \(D\) need not be a field or reduced, especially when the residue characteristic divides \(e\).

42. “Computed once … with \(q\) a free variable” is not literally explained by \(D\), since \(\kappa\), characteristic-dependent binomial cancellation, and \(\bar z\) are not objects over a formal variable \(q\). A universal algebraic framework or case-indexing mechanism is missing.

43. The pattern packet omits all digit values while later transition behavior depends on expressions involving \(\bar z\) and transported digits. The stability implication \((\star)\) therefore bears substantially more content than the description suggests; its exact equivalence relation must be given.

44. The displayed pattern bound and read bound are arithmetically well-formed, but “rank,” “run-collapsed read,” “letter,” and “distinct” are undefined. The catalogue numbers cannot be independently interpreted from this page.

45. The linear recursion
   \[
   m_N=Km_{N-1}+b
   \]
   needs the initialization \(m_0=0\). With that convention,
   \[
   m_N=\sum_{d=0}^{N-1}K^db
   \]
   and the infinite resolvent formula are correct when \(\rho(K)<1\).

46. Splitting a cluster into multiple independent subclusters naturally gives convolutions of types, not immediately a linear transition on single-cluster states. The account must explain whether smaller degrees are already solved inductively or whether states include accumulated multisets of pieces.

47. The scalar geometric series is correct:
   \[
   \sum_{j\ge0}q^{-Ej}
   =\frac1{1-q^{-E}}
   =\frac{q^E}{q^E-1}.
   \]

48. The complete degree-\(2\) enumeration is correct: the three reduction counts sum to
   \[
   \frac{q(q-1)}2+\frac{q^2-q}2+q=q^2.
   \]

49. The degree-\(2\) cluster strata are correct. Conditional on \(v(b),v(c)\ge1\), the event \(v(c)=1\) has mass \(1-q^{-1}\), while \(v(c)\ge2\) has mass \(q^{-1}\), and division after \(x=py\) restores independent uniform coefficients.

50. The two-state quadratic solve is fully consistent. Inverting
   \[
   I-K=
   \begin{pmatrix}1&-q^{-1}\\-q^{-1}&1\end{pmatrix}
   \]
   gives determinant \(1-q^{-2}\), and the displayed solutions reduce exactly to
   \[
   \rho_{\rm ram}=\frac1{q+1},\qquad
   \rho_{\rm split}=\rho_{\rm inert}=\frac{q}{2(q+1)}.
   \]

51. Calling the root–cluster–root circuit a “self-loop” is graphically inaccurate: it is a two-edge cycle in the displayed two-state graph. It becomes a self-loop only after an additional state elimination or run collapse that is not shown.

52. There is a logical tension in Movement 4. If \(\det(I-K)\) really factors blockwise only into terms \(1-q^{-E}\), it is automatically nonzero for every \(q\ge2\), so determinant nonvanishing cannot remain an open regularity clause. Conversely, if more general determinant factors occur, closure of the solve in the stated ring does not follow from the elementary argument given.

53. Substochasticity plus \(\det(I-K)\ne0\) does imply \(\rho(K)<1\): Perron–Frobenius makes \(1\) an eigenvalue whenever a nonnegative substochastic matrix has spectral radius \(1\). This part is correct.

54. The identity
   \[
   (I-K)\sum_{d=0}^{N-1}K^d=I-K^N
   \]
   and the resulting tail formula are algebraically correct.

55. The exact identification
   \[
   \frac{D_\sigma(N)}{p^{nN}}
   =\left[\sum_{d=0}^{N-1}K^db_\sigma\right]_{\rm root}
   \]
   is not justified by the preceding construction. A graph transition can pin several digits, while \(N\) on the left is coefficient precision. Graph-step depth and \(p\)-adic level have been conflated unless the matrix is graded by digit cost.

56. For the same reason, the assertion that \(K^N\) is exactly “mass deciding after level \(N\)” needs a level-preserving theorem, not merely pattern stability.

57. Given that missing identification, the subsequent inequalities and capstone bracket are algebraically correct:
   \[
   0\le R_\sigma-\frac{D_\sigma(N)}{p^{nN}}\le\varepsilon_N
   \]
   rearranges to the displayed two-sided count bound.

58. The degree-\(2\) undecided-envelope paragraph contains a textual deletion:
   “If \(d\not\equiv0\ldots\), the type is decided: \(k=v(d)\) The skeleton…”
   At least one sentence or clause is missing.

59. At odd \(p\), the intended exact count \(U(N)/p^{2N}=q^{-N}\) is correct because the discriminant is uniform and undecidedness is exactly \(d\equiv0\bmod p^N\).

60. The \(p=2\) bound is internally correct:
   \[
   \frac12\,2^{-(N-3)}=4\,2^{-N}.
   \]
   The explanation should distinguish “sufficient information by level \(k+4\)” from an exact decision threshold.

61. The coarse certified bound is numerically consistent:
   at \(p=2,N=9\),
   \[
   \left(\left\lfloor\frac92\right\rfloor+1\right)2^{-8}
   =\frac5{256}.
   \]

62. The degree-\(5\) tame walk refers to an absent cubic table, so the displayed cubic recursion is not derivable solely from this page. Its algebra is nevertheless correct:
   \[
   \frac{(1-q^{-1})(1+q^{-2})}{1-q^{-5}}
   =\frac{q^2(q^2+1)}{q^4+q^3+q^2+q+1}.
   \]

63. The value
   \[
   \beta_5[\sigma]
   \]
   is simply asserted. No strata or recursion producing its numerator and denominator are displayed, despite the section promising “two walks in full.” Consequently, its derivation cannot be checked from the supplied text.

64. Assuming the asserted \(\beta_5[\sigma]\), the combination of the three mod-\(p\) families is algebraically correct and simplifies to the stated tame degree-\(5\) function.

65. The stated tame numerical evaluations are correct:
   \[
   R(2)=\frac{572}{11811}\approx0.04843,\quad
   R(3)=\frac{15849}{529012}\approx0.02996,
   \]
   \[
   R(5)=\frac{629875}{45761133}\approx0.01376,\quad
   R(7)=\frac{23951347}{3075654856}\approx0.007787.
   \]

66. The denominator-provenance sentence is too compressed. The final factors are \(\Phi_2(q)\Phi_5(q)\Phi_7(q)\), but explaining exactly how the \(q^{14}-1\) loop loses its \(q^7+1\) part requires cancellations not exhibited by the walk.

67. The wild quintic stratum masses are internally consistent. Relative to the initial cluster, the four slopes cost respectively \(0,3,6,9\) additional digits, and the rescaling condition costs
   \[
   4+3+2+1=10
   \]
   additional digits.

68. The wild quintic circuit weight
   \[
   q^{-10}q^{-4}=q^{-14}
   \]
   is correct.

69. The wild geometric expansion and simplification are correct:
   \[
   q^{-4}(1-q^{-1})(1+q^{-3}+q^{-6}+q^{-9})
   \frac1{1-q^{-14}}
   =
   \frac{(q-1)(q^3+1)(q^6+1)}{q^{14}-1}.
   \]

70. Its exact evaluations are also correct:
   \[
   R(2)=\frac{195}{5461},\quad
   R(3)=\frac{5110}{597871},\quad
   R(5)=\frac{328146}{254313151},
   \]
   \[
   R(7)=\frac{5058950}{14129647351}.
   \]

71. “One factor per circuit digit” is inaccurate wording. The factor \(q^{14}-1\) records a circuit that pins fourteen digits; it is not one denominator factor for each digit.

72. The claim that a unit of \(\mathbb Z_5\) is a fifth power “exactly when its image mod \(25\) is one” is false as written. General fifth powers may reduce modulo \(25\) to any Teichmüller lift of a nonzero residue, not only to \(1\). The statement is true only after normalizing to a principal unit congruent to \(1\bmod5\).

73. The notation
   \[
   R_\sigma(1/q)\sim R_\sigma(q)
   \]
   uses an undefined relation \(\sim\). The later prose suggests equality up to a specified monomial \(q^{w_\sigma}\), but neither the exponent nor its dependence on \(\sigma\) is defined.

74. The example
   \[
   R_{\rm ram}(1/q)=qR_{\rm ram}(q)
   \]
   is correct, but one example does not define the claimed general functional equation.

75. The external attributions—“Chebotarev paper,” arXiv:2212.00294, Guàrdia–Montes–Nart Theorem 4.18, Del Corso–Dvornicich, and “Denef–Igusa cell decomposition”—lack enough bibliographic and proposition-level information for a fresh reader to determine exactly which imported statements support which claims.

76. The final claim that “everything else on this page is proved” conflicts with several earlier qualifications: the degree-\(5\) values are computations rather than certificates, the carry-facing stability statement is conditional, the determinant condition is open, and thirteen hypotheses are not yet formulated. Even with the ledger, “everything else” is too broad.
